concerns.text: The statistical model (Fixed‑Effects ANOVA or Kruskal‑Wallis) is applied to only nine observations (3 methods × 3 datasets). This sample size is far too small to reliably estimate variance components, meet normality/homogeneity assumptions, or achieve adequate statistical power for detecting method effects.

Dataset identity is not modeled as a random effect (the original mixed‑effects specification was replaced). Consequently, any systematic differences between the three GEO datasets (e.g., cell‑type composition, sequencing depth) are confounded with the ‘method’ factor, violating the assumption that method effects are independent of dataset characteristics.

Leiden clustering resolution is optimized per embedding by maximizing the Silhouette Score before computing ARI/NMI. This data‑driven selection inflates fidelity metrics and introduces selection bias, making the subsequent ANOVA comparison of methods invalid because the response variable is no longer a fixed measurement but a function of the method‑specific optimization.

The plan states it will “test the effect of `method` on fidelity,” implying a causal interpretation. The design is purely observational (each dataset is processed with all methods) and lacks random assignment or control of other covariates, so causal claims about method superiority are not justified.
